construction: Unchanged globally self-consistent exponential midpoint: each frozen-stage sector applies exp(-i h_s dt/2) to the original boundary, reduces n_s and positive g_s with original complex D_s, then the parent sums in the original slot order and evaluates K only after every sector. Final exp(-i h_s dt) frames are saved independently; boundary publication follows successful completion of every frame.
execution: Linux fork ProcessPoolExecutor isolation, not threads: shared input pages are copy-on-write, every cache/factory/action is process-private. Fork occurs only from a single-threaded caller with native BLAS/OpenMP limited to one thread by threadpoolctl and startup environment. One explicitly supplied CPU in 6..10 per worker. At most worker-count tasks/results are outstanding in each map batch. Final full frames stay in workers and are written directly to their unique files. Parent reduction order is deterministic. Global H0 call reservations and all work counters share a multiprocessing lock. Exceptions stop submission and prevent boundary publication; executor shutdown waits for already running members of the bounded batch. Complete boundary JSON is atomically linked only after all frames succeed.
identity: Physical identity hashes only aggregate, manifest, preparation, initial ions and the scalar definition. Execution implementation/oracle and numerical controls remain provenance. Only the exact known digest-bound t=0 boundary and old model identity may be adopted; old physical specification, unchanged initial ions, complete authenticated frame/D bindings and all slot identities must match. Adoption writes only a new boundary, retains the old one, and reuses all frame/D bytes. No nonzero-time cross-model migration.

Time operator construction, action, prepared moments and full-frame exponential separately, with explicit H0 cap and interval. Report ru_maxrss and /proc memory; no full-material trajectory or collective rate inference.
